messages:
eve_customer: Hi team — we have a paying customer hitting a weird Safari-only issue for their EventSource stream via the CDN. It consistently drops after ~48–65s with partial events delivered. Direct origin (no CDN) works. Repro steps below.

Doris_QA: can you paste a minimal repro (headers + console logs)?

eve_customer: Repro: open https://cdn.redwood.example/stream?session=XXX in Safari 15.6, wait ~1min. Network pane shows the response, tokens come in for a while then stop. Console: "EventSource error". curl to origin vs cdn: (note origin=stream.redwood.internal)

```
# CDN (problem)
$ curl -i -N "https://cdn.redwood.example/stream?session=XXX"
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Cache-Control: max-age=0
Vary: Accept-Encoding

: first chunk\n\nid: 1\ndata: {\"partial\":true}\n\n# stops after ~55s

# Origin (ok)
$ curl -i -N "https://stream.redwood.internal/stream?session=XXX"
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Cache-Control: no-store, no-transform

: heartbeat\n\nid: 1\ndata: {\"complete\":true}\n\n# keeps streaming
```

alice_support: this smells like CDN revalidation/edge caching interfering midstream. Safari historically closes EventSource if it sees a 304 or mismatch in content-length/chunking, or if intermediate proxies change encoding. Also service workers can break streaming.

ben_frontend: can you reproduce with `--no-buffer` and force bypass CDN (hosts hack)? try `curl -i -N -H 'Cache-Control: no-cache' https://stream.redwood.internal/stream` and also try a plain browser GET to origin.

carlos_platform: I checked the edge logs for that session id — edge revalidated the origin after ~60s and responded 304 to the client when origin answered conditional GET. The client saw the stream disappear (edge log: 200 -> 304 revalidate). On our CDN config the streaming route is still in route table with `max-age=0` which causes revalidation. Edge also sometimes rewrites `Vary` and strips `Authorization` on cached responses.

doris_qa: we tried patching staging to set `Cache-Control: no-store` for `/stream` and added explicit `Vary: Authorization, Cookie`. Staging results: Safari kept the connection open for 10+ minutes during our run, no midstream 304.

alice_support: notes for customers/short-term mitigation: instruct CDN to treat `/stream` as non-cacheable (Cache-Control: no-store / private), disable revalidate/conditional caching for that route, and ensure the CDN does not gzip/chunk coalesce SSE payloads. Add `Cache-Control: no-transform` to avoid edge modifying body. Also ensure `Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8` and `Connection: keep-alive`.

ben_frontend: additional app-level workarounds: add heartbeat comments from server every 20–25s (e.g., `:hb\n\n`) so Safari knows the connection is alive. For customers with SWs, ensure the SW does NOT intercept /stream. Example in SW: `if (new URL(event.request.url).pathname.startsWith('/stream')) return fetch(event.request);`

eve_customer: we do have a service worker that caches GETs. Could that be the cause?

carlos_platform: yes — SW can buffer and then return a cached response or revalidate causing a 304. Make SW explicitly bypass streaming endpoints. Also header-level fixes are safer: origin should always return 200 for streaming and avoid ETag/Last-Modified on that route.

doris_qa: polyfills: users using `eventsource-polyfill` (xhr-based polyfill) sometimes see different behavior — polyfill will buffer based on XHR streaming support and can hang on Safari variants. Where possible prefer native EventSource with CDN passthrough.

ben_frontend: small JS snippet to detect and log readyState and errors for debugging:```js
const es = new EventSource('/stream?session=XXX');
es.onmessage = e => console.log('msg', e.data);
es.onerror = e => console.log('es error', es.readyState, e);
setInterval(() => console.log('rs', es.readyState), 10000);
```

alice_support: action plan we applied on staging: 1) set `Cache-Control: no-store, no-transform` on streaming route 2) add `Vary: Authorization, Cookie` 3) disable ETag on that route 4) ensure server flushes a `:heartbeat` every 20s 5) instruct SW to bypass.

deploy-bot: Deployed streaming header patch to staging at 2026-03-16T22:12Z (rollout=staging).

doris_qa: QA run (30m) — passing on staging Safari 13–16, no disconnects observed. Will schedule 10% canary to prod tomorrow AM.

eve_customer: thanks, we tried staging (via customer test account) and initial runs look good. We'll validate under load tomorrow and report back. Any guidance for customers behind Akamai/CloudFront?

carlos_platform: for Akamai/CloudFront explicitly configure the behavior for path to never revalidate (no conditional requests). On CloudFront use Cache Policy that sets TTL=0 but `Origin Request Policy` to forward all headers and `CacheBasedOnSelectedHeaders=Whitelist` with Authorization/Cookie. Akamai: set `Edge-Control: no-store` for the route. Document these in a KB article.

alice_support: follow-ups: I'll open a KB with these steps, include the curl repro commands, SW snippet, and recommended headers. Marking this thread as escalated -> edge team until canary completes. :thumbsup:

eve_customer: appreciated — will confirm tomorrow.
